policy: Reservoir records describe ecological evidence and known host-virus relationships. Reservoir distribution does not mean infected animals are present at a site, and it does not mean human cases have occurred there.

reservoirs.associatedVirus: Sin Nombre virus and related North American hantaviruses
reservoirs.primarySyndrome: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome / hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome
reservoirs.evidenceRegion: Much of North America, with important U.S. western and Four Corners context
reservoirs.mapRegion: Western and broad North America reservoir context
reservoirs.summary: CDC and state health agencies identify deer mice as the main U.S. reservoir associated with Sin Nombre virus, the most common cause of HPS in the United States.
limitations: Seeing a deer mouse does not prove it is infected.
Reservoir distribution is ecological context, not a human case map.

reservoirs.summary: CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases lists white-footed mouse as the rodent reservoir for New York virus.
limitations: Reservoir evidence does not provide public human case locations.
This MVP does not model infection prevalence in rodents.

reservoirs.summary: CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases lists cotton rat as the rodent reservoir for Black Creek Canal virus.
limitations: Host species distribution is not a measure of human risk at a property.
This MVP does not publish rodent testing results.

reservoirs.evidenceRegion: Southeastern United States and Gulf Coast ecological context
reservoirs.mapRegion: Gulf Coast and southeastern United States
reservoirs.summary: CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases lists rice rat as the rodent reservoir for Bayou virus.
limitations: A reservoir range should not be interpreted as a current outbreak area.
This MVP does not infer county-level human cases from reservoir ecology.

reservoirs.primarySyndrome: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome / nephropathia epidemica
reservoirs.mapRegion: Northern, central, and parts of eastern Europe
reservoirs.summary: ECDC describes Puumala virus, carried by bank voles, as the most frequent cause of notified orthohantavirus infections in Europe.
limitations: European HFRS surveillance is different from U.S. HPS reporting.
Rodent abundance and human case reporting fluctuate over time.

reservoirs.associatedVirus: Andes virus and other New World hantaviruses
reservoirs.evidenceRegion: South America, including Southern Cone countries
reservoirs.mapRegion: Southern Cone ecological and surveillance context
reservoirs.summary: WHO describes Andes virus as a South American hantavirus for which limited person-to-person transmission has been documented among close contacts, while primary acquisition remains linked to rodent exposure.
limitations: This record does not map specific rodent species ranges.
Limited Andes virus person-to-person transmission is event-specific and should not be generalized to all hantaviruses.
